cards.title: What this repo ships
items: this repository ships the contract, not a running service: three Agent Skills (j2ee-best-practices, j2ee-review, j2ee-port) plus a drop-in Checkstyle config in lints/

the skills carry the digests (references/jakarta-ee.md, j2ee-architecture.md, j2ee-patterns.md) that the diagram above describes; the Java template under src/main/java/com/example/app/ is the worked example of the same contract

the machine half is CI: check.yml runs the skill validator, the Java-example balance gate, the unittest suite, and — on Ubuntu with a JDK — javac + the self-check plus the Checkstyle violation harness

cards.title: The runtime contract
items: apps/api and apps/worker are the only composition roots: CDI producers return the port type, never the implementation, and business code never reaches for a BeanManager
the use case owns the JTA transaction — not the resource, not the repository — so a failure leaves no partial effect; there is no XA, a distributed effect is an idempotent async job

JPA entities live in adapters and never cross the API: the edge returns DTO records, and the error envelope is {error:{code,message,requiredPermission,correlationId}} with one ExceptionMapper per family

cards.title: Tenant isolation, twice
items: tenant_id NOT NULL on every table, first in every index and first in every predicate; the use case checks permission and ownership before the write
the database is the second line: PostgreSQL row-level security with a dedicated non-bypass application role, app.tenant_id set per transaction by the adapter, migrations under a separate owner role
a two-tenant test — a query without the predicate returns zero rows, a cross-tenant write fails — is a release blocker, not a nice-to-have

cards.title: The async path
items: the outbox row and the domain row commit in one JTA transaction; a separate commit for the event loses it
the worker polls due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishes through JMS or HTTP, and marks the row sent; a bounded job carries a batch size, a time budget, a backoff and a dead-letter row
JMS is at-least-once, so every consumer is idempotent and deduplicates by the idempotency key; the message carries tenantId, correlationId and the key
